title: Evaluation coherence of generic stratum-Hom exchange
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ be an immersion, with fixed closed-then-open factorization, and let $s':S'\hookrightarrow X'$ be its cartesian pullback along a scheme morphism $g_X:X'\to X$, with $g_S:S'\to S$ [def-pc-base-change, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use $Rs_!,Rs^!,Rs_*$ and their primed versions from these factorizations, with $Rs_!=j_!i_*$ and $Rs^!=Ri^!j^*$ [lem-cbc-open-closed-recollement, lem-exc-closed-ambient]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], derived tensor $\otimes_A^L$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and derived internal Hom $\mathscr H_T(U,V)=R\mathcal Hom_{A_T}(U,V)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Scheme inverse images on these categories are exact constant-coefficient inverse images [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Let $P\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, and $H=\mathscr H_S(P,Rs^!M)$. Write $b:g_X^*Rs_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rs'_!g_S^*$ for canonical extension-by-zero base change, $e:g_X^*Rs_*\to Rs'_*g_S^*$ for the adjunction-mate exchange, and $a:g_S^*Rs^!M\to Rs'^!g_X^*M$ for a comparison satisfying the exceptional counit identity
$$\varepsilon^!_{s',g_X^*M}\circ Rs'_!(a)\circ b_{Rs^!M}=g_X^*\varepsilon^!_{s,M}.$$
Assume the canonical projection isomorphisms commute with $g^*$ under $b$ [lem-sf-etale-generic-immersion-projection]. Use the evaluation-normalized isomorphisms $\theta_s,\theta_{s'}$ of [lem-sf-etale-generic-stratum-mate], and let $\beta_{P,Rs^!M}$ be the transpose of pulled-back evaluation. Then the composite
$$g_X^*\mathscr H_X(Rs_!P,M)\xrightarrow{g_X^*\theta_s}g_X^*Rs_*H\xrightarrow{e_H}Rs'_*g_S^*H\xrightarrow{Rs'_*\beta_{P,Rs^!M}}Rs'_*\mathscr H_{S'}(g_S^*P,g_S^*Rs^!M)\xrightarrow{Rs'_*\mathscr H(1,a)}Rs'_*\mathscr H_{S'}(g_S^*P,Rs'^!g_X^*M)\xrightarrow{\theta_{s'}^{-1}}\mathscr H_{X'}(Rs'_!g_S^*P,g_X^*M)$$
has tensor transpose $g_X^*\mathrm{ev}_{Rs_!P,M}$ after identifying its tensor input by $b_P$ and the canonical tensor pullback map. Thus it equals the canonical evaluation-induced comparison $\beta_{Rs_!P,M}$. This assertion is an identity of maps and assumes no isomorphism property of $e_H$, $a$, or $\beta_{P,Rs^!M}$.

proof.text:
Write $F=Rs_!$, $R=Rs_*$, $q=s^*$, $F'=Rs'_!$, $R'=Rs'_*$, $q'=s'^*$, $T=g_X^*$ and $U=g_S^*$. Let $\chi:q'T\xrightarrow{\sim}Uq$ be the canonical inverse-image square isomorphism, $N=Rs^!M$, $H=\mathscr H_S(P,N)$ and $C=\mathscr H_X(FP,M)$. All tensors below are derived over $A$. The ringed-site closed adjunction [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] fixes evaluation and its natural transposition bijection on these unbounded categories. Put $u=\theta_s:C\to RH$, let $t=\varepsilon^*_{s,H}\circ q(u):qC\to H$ be its ordinary inverse/direct-image adjoint, and put $d=\mathrm{ev}_{P,N}\circ(t\otimes1_P):qC\otimes P\to N$. Apply the characterization in [lem-sf-etale-generic-stratum-mate] to this $u$. Since $\theta_s^{-1}u=1_C$, its tensor transpose is evaluation, giving
$$\mathrm{ev}_{FP,M}=\varepsilon^!_{s,M}\circ F(d)\circ\pi_{s,C,P}.$$
Here $C,P,M$ are arbitrary ambient complexes, as allowed by both citations.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), equation 08J8 (equation-internal-hom); agent expansion of the cartesian mate and exceptional counit calculation.

proof.text:
The adjoint of $e_H\circ T(u):TC\to R'UH$ under $q'\dashv R'$ is exactly
$$\varepsilon^{*}_{s',UH}\circ q'(e_H)\circ q'T(u)=U(t)\circ\chi_C.$$
Indeed [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] defines the exchange as the transpose of $U(\varepsilon^{*}_{s,H})\circ\chi_{RH}$. Substituting this in the left side and using naturality of $\chi$ at $u$ gives $U(\varepsilon^{*}_{s,H})\circ Uq(u)\circ\chi_C=U(t)\circ\chi_C$. This uses no invertibility of $e_H$.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), equation 08J8 (equation-internal-hom); agent expansion of the cartesian mate and exceptional counit calculation.

proof.text:
Put $P'=UP$, $N'=Rs'^!TM$ and
$$v=\mathscr H_{S'}(1,a)\circ\beta_{P,N}\circ U(t)\circ\chi_C:q'TC\to\mathscr H_{S'}(P',N').$$
Let $m_U:U(qC)\otimes UP\xrightarrow{\sim}U(qC\otimes P)$ be the inverse tensor comparison supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The tensor transpose of $v$ is
$$d'=a\circ U(d)\circ m_U\circ(\chi_C\otimes1_{UP}).$$
To check this, naturality of the closed adjunction in its last variable [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] gives $\mathrm{ev}_{P',N'}\circ(\mathscr H(1,a)\otimes1)=a\circ\mathrm{ev}_{P',UN}$. The defining equation for $\beta_{P,N}$ gives $\mathrm{ev}_{P',UN}\circ(\beta_{P,N}\otimes1)=U(\mathrm{ev}_{P,N})\circ m_U$, now with $H$ in the first tensor input. Precompose with $U(t)\chi_C\otimes1$; naturality of the tensor comparison moves $U(t)\otimes1$ through $m_U$, yielding the displayed $d'$ by the definition of $d$.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), equation 08J8 (equation-internal-hom); agent expansion of the cartesian mate and exceptional counit calculation.

proof.text:
Let $\Phi$ be the composite asserted in the statement, a map $TC\to\mathscr H_{X'}(F'UP,TM)$. By step 2 and naturality of the ordinary adjunction in its target, the ordinary adjoint of
$$R'\mathscr H(1,a)\circ R'\beta_{P,N}\circ e_H\circ T(u)$$
is $v$ of step 3. Apply [lem-sf-etale-generic-stratum-mate] to $s'$, the test object $TC$, the input $UP$ and the target $TM$. Its formula therefore says that the tensor transpose $w:TC\otimes F'UP\to TM$ of $\Phi$ is
$$w=\varepsilon^!_{s',TM}\circ F'(d')\circ\pi_{s',TC,UP}.$$
All four objects lie in the stated ordinary unbounded derived categories; the cited characterization has no finiteness assumption on them.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), equation 08J8 (equation-internal-hom); agent expansion of the cartesian mate and exceptional counit calculation.

proof.text:
We identify $TC\otimes TFP$ with $T(C\otimes FP)$ by the inverse tensor comparison. Projection compatibility [lem-sf-etale-generic-immersion-projection] is the following typed equality:
$$F'\bigl(m_U\circ(\chi_C\otimes1_{UP})\bigr)\circ\pi_{s',TC,UP}\circ(1_{TC}\otimes b_P)=b_{qC\otimes P}\circ T(\pi_{s,C,P}).$$
The pullback composition identifications in this equality respect tensor comparisons by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], applied to the equality $g_Xs'=sg_S$ of morphisms of constant-$A$ ringed topoi. Thus no independently chosen tensor or square isomorphism is inserted. Substitute step 3 in step 4 and use this equality. Naturality of the canonical base-change transformation $b$ at $d:qC\otimes P\to N$ gives $F'(Ud)\circ b_{qC\otimes P}=b_N\circ T(Fd)$. Consequently
$$w\circ(1\otimes b_P)=\varepsilon^!_{s',TM}\circ F'(a)\circ b_N\circ T(Fd)\circ T(\pi_{s,C,P}).$$

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), equation 08J8 (equation-internal-hom); agent expansion of the cartesian mate and exceptional counit calculation.

proof.text:
The assumed exceptional counit identity is $\varepsilon^!_{s',TM}\circ F'(a)\circ b_N=T(\varepsilon^!_{s,M})$. Inserting it in the last display and using functoriality of $T$, followed by the evaluation identity of step 1, yields
$$w\circ(1\otimes b_P)=T\bigl(\varepsilon^!_{s,M}\circ F(d)\circ\pi_{s,C,P}\bigr)=T(\mathrm{ev}_{FP,M}).$$
This is precisely the claimed pulled-back tensor transpose, with the specified input identification. The bijection in [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] is injective, so $\Phi=\beta_{FP,M}$, where the latter is defined by that transpose. Only the isomorphisms $b$ and the tensor comparisons were inverted; none of $e_H$, $a$ or $\beta_{P,N}$ was inverted. The calculation also applies when the stratum or either complex is zero.
